The main risk is that water is hypotonic, so it can be absorbed into the circulation through the bladder wall, especially if the bladder mucosa is damaged. This can cause fluid overload and hyponatraemia, and osmotic haemolysis of red cells that may lead to acute kidney injury. The team note's claim, that the main risk is water leaking around the catheter because it is thicker than saline, is wrong. Water is not more viscous than saline, so sterile 0.9% sodium chloride is used instead.

CONFIDENCE: 85
